clue.text: Brief, politically, suits premier

blocks.note: rhyming slang: 'whistle and flute' means suit, so suits are whistles
the premier thing is the top one

explanation.surface: A short political memo says the prime minister approves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like a noun (a lawyer's brief) but is the adjective of the definition. Whistle and flute is Cockney rhyming slang for a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle-stop tour is a rapid campaign trip by a politician, pausing only briefly at each small town.

clue.text: Potential victims, punched, keel over

blocks.note: to punch is to hit
a ship that lists leans over to one side

explanation.surface: Targets get punched and fall over.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit list names the people someone intends to kill or attack, so it is a roster of targets.

clue.text: Untouchable item in bag, shade lower

blocks.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
red is a shade of colour
read as one who lows, a mooing beast

explanation.surface: A precious object in a bag, its colour toned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like the verb to reduce, but it rhymes with 'mower': something that lows, or moos.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea or institution held to be beyond criticism, like the animal revered in Hinduism.

clue.text: Run away, far from criminal!

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: to flee on foot in British slang
second meaning, as one word: lawful and genuine

explanation.surface: Someone flees the scene while protesting they are no crook.
explanation.walkthrough: To leg it is British slang for to run off; the same letters make the informal adjective for legitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is a casual shortening of legitimate, meaning lawful and above board, the opposite of crooked.

clue.text: Troublemaker, one with a spoon?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who deliberately causes discord
second meaning, taken literally: a person mixing a pot

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is taken literally, one who mixes liquid round with a spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stirs up trouble is said to stir, so mischief-making gossip and cooking share one verb.

clue.text: A once mysterious island area in Pacific region

indicators.note: something mysterious is puzzling and obscure, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
I is the abbreviation for island on maps
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A formerly mysterious island somewhere in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the geographical name for Australia, New Zealand and the islands of the central and south Pacific.

clue.text: Stubble forming on adult male initially, obliged to go in — for this?

definitions.text: Stubble forming on adult male initially, obliged to go in — for this?

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the words before it
going in means one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words
obliged to do something is having to do it

explanation.surface: A grown man's growing stubble means he must lather up before shaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the question 'for this?' asks what a stubbly man must use.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaving foam is the lather a man spreads on his face before razoring off his whiskers.

clue.text: Nick is working under electoral system

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the words before it below the final piece

blocks.note: PR stands for proportional representation
taken as written
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Nick works within the voting arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, the nick is a jail or police station, a place of custody.

clue.text: Either radical ahead of Conservative dissenter

indicators.note: radical change overturns the existing order, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A party member on either the left or the right breaks with the Tory line.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds opinions opposed to accepted doctrine, which is exactly what a dissenter does.

clue.text: Wild tiger has gripped a protective covering for leg

indicators.note: wild suggests something unruly and out of order, so the next word is jumbled
to grip something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild tiger has seized someone, and their leg protection is all that saved them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaiter is a cloth or leather sheath worn over the ankle and lower shin, shielding it from mud.

clue.text: That male character will follow infant very closely

indicators.note: following means coming after, so those words are placed behind the first piece

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
the pronoun for that man
a character of the alphabet is a letter

explanation.surface: A man of character will closely follow a small child around.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow instructions to the letter is to obey them exactly, missing out no detail.

clue.text: Trace item of underwear, oddly in grey

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered positions of the words that follow

blocks.note: a vest is a garment worn under a shirt in Britain
the first, third and fifth letters of the two words run together

explanation.surface: Searching for a hint of a grey undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' runs across both words, 'in' as well as 'grey', so 'in' is not a container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a small remaining sign of something that has otherwise disappeared, a mere remnant.

clue.text: North American city also welcoming leader of revolution, not surprisingly

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the other pieces go inside
the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept
a surprising result is an unexpected arrangement, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: too means as well
the opening letter of the word
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A city also welcoming a revolutionary leader, which surprises nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not surprisingly' reads as one phrase meaning 'naturally', but 'not' is the fodder and 'surprisingly' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada and the capital of Ontario province.

clue.text: Musical group I observed in testament

indicators.note: something observed in a place is seen inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: NT is the usual abbreviation for New Testament
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A band I watched appear in a will or in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is an ensemble of nine performers, or a piece written for nine instruments.

clue.text: Pest in male fish

blocks.note: a cock is a male bird
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Some parasite has got into a male fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts one thing inside another but merely links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockroaches are scuttling insects that infest kitchens, a classic household vermin.

clue.text: The present time?

blocks.note: surface reading: now, the current moment
setter's reading: a present is a gift, so this is the gift-giving season of the year

explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as 'current' but means a gift; the question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive season of December 25th is when people exchange gifts with family and friends.

clue.text: Might I prefer half of wood chopped up?

indicators.note: half means only part of the following word is taken, here its front portion
chopping something up breaks it into pieces that can be reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the first two of its four letters

explanation.surface: Someone muses whether they would rather have only half the timber chopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' sits first like a modal verb opening a question, but it is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Firepower is the destructive capacity of an army's weapons, hence force or strength in general.

clue.text: Put right or else wrong, victory secured

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its proper order, so the letters before it are rearranged
something secured is held firmly in place inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
V is the abbreviation for victory

explanation.surface: Fix things or else go wrong, with the win already in the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve a problem is to settle or fix it, setting matters straight.

clue.text: Drop fruit on police

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the next

blocks.note: a plum is a fruit
the Met is the Metropolitan Police of London

explanation.surface: Someone is told to let some fruit fall on the officers below.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply and fast, a sudden plunge.

clue.text: Part blew over backwards, I say

indicators.note: part means the answer is only a portion of the words that follow
backwards tells us to read those letters from right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Something partly blew over in the wind, an exclaiming onlooker remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' sounds like an exclamation of surprise; read it as 'I, for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter I is one of the five vowel letters, so it serves as an example of the class.

clue.text: Unremarkable article in large residence

indicators.note: in places the word before it inside the following one

blocks.note: a villa is a large country house
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A plain, ordinary item found in a grand mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain vanilla, after the basic ice cream flavour, means ordinary with no special features.

clue.text: Everything absorbed by saturated pouch

indicators.note: something absorbed is soaked up and held within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: saturated means soaking wet
all means everything

explanation.surface: A soaked purse has soaked up everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a flat folding case for banknotes and cards, a small holder carried in a pocket.

clue.text: A sailor reported crime

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how it sounds

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman has notified the police of an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Assault, an attack or threat of violence against a person, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Poisonous beef consumed by little jerk

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a tic is a small involuntary twitch
beef cattle are oxen

explanation.surface: A small brat ate some tainted beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little jerk' suggests a small nasty person but is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something toxic contains harmful substances that can sicken or kill, so it is venomous.

clue.text: Underwear tight at first after manoeuvring legs in

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before
after places one piece behind the other in the answer
manoeuvring things moves them around into new positions

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone wriggles their legs into tight-fitting underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest worn under a shirt or for athletics, so it counts as an undergarment.

clue.text: Peak in cold capital city, unknown

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Lima is the capital of Peru
x is the algebraic symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: A mountain summit somewhere in a chilly capital, location unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the highest or most intense point of something, its culmination.

clue.text: Islander, man transporting group back

indicators.note: a vehicle transporting something carries it inside, so one piece holds the other
back tells us to read the word before it in the other direction

blocks.note: a man is a male
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: An island resident drives a band home again.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Malta, the Mediterranean island nation, is called Maltese.

clue.text: Protestant writer travelling to castle

indicators.note: travelling things are moved about, so these letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Protestant author journeys to a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but here it is the instrument a writer holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecostal churches form a branch of evangelical Protestant Christianity emphasising gifts of the Holy Spirit.
